name: Methi Bajra Puri
subtitle: millet and fenugreek puris, crisp-edged and faintly bitter

ingredients.note: binds the millet — bajra alone will not roll into a puri

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp for the dough, plus 600ml for frying

prepNotes: Toss the chopped methi with 1/2 tsp salt and leave 10 minutes, then squeeze hard. This pulls out the water and much of the bitterness.
Knead with warm water — bajra needs the heat to come together, even with the wheat flour in it.
Rest the dough 15 minutes before rolling, no longer; the methi keeps weeping and the dough goes slack.

steps.text: Squeeze the salted methi dry and put it in a bowl with both flours, ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, sesame and salt.
Rub in the 2 tbsp oil, then add warm water a little at a time to make a stiff dough, firmer than chapati dough.
steps.tip: Stiff dough gives puffed puris; soft dough soaks up oil.

steps.text: Knead 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide into 16 balls and roll each into a 10cm disc on a lightly oiled surface, about 3mm thick.
steps.tip: Oil the surface rather than dusting with flour — loose flour burns and blackens the frying oil.

steps.text: Heat the oil to 180C. A scrap of dough should rise to the surface in about 2 seconds.
Slide in one puri, press it under with the back of a slotted spoon for 3 seconds until it puffs.
Flip and fry the second side 30-40 seconds until the edges are crisp and the colour is deep brown-green.
steps.tip: Bajra puris go darker than wheat ones — judge by the crisp edge, not the colour.

steps.text: Drain upright in a colander so the oil runs off, and serve hot with aloo pyaaz ki sabzi or plain yogurt.

storage: Best within 2-3 hours. They soften as they cool; keep 2 days in an airtight tin and crisp for 5 minutes in a 180C oven before serving.
